<!DOCTYPE html>
<!--
================================================================================
  REPORT: Kit Availability
  PATH:   Product/KitAvailability.htm
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Interactive HTML rebuild of the custom JasperReports report
  C:\Program Files\Fishbowl\server\reports\Custom\Kit Availability.jrxml,
  on the shared fb-lib / fb-styles stack. Skeleton and conventions follow
  Manufacturing/AvailableToBuild.htm, which answers the same question for BOMs.

  WHAT IT ANSWERS
    For each kit product (product.kitFlag = 1) in the selected location
    group(s): how many complete kits could be assembled and sold right now
    from current inventory. The scarcest kit line is the bottleneck.

  CORE MATH
    Per kit x location group, over the kit lines that can constrain it:
        qtyPerKit_base   = kititem.defaultQty * uomconversion.multiply / factor
                           (kititem.uomId -> part.uomId)
        perLineKits      = FLOOR( availableForSale_base / qtyPerKit_base )
        Kits Available   = MIN(perLineKits)   (floored at 0)

  AVAILABILITY BASIS = "Available for Sale" (matches the .jrxml):
        OnHand - Allocated - NotAvailable + DropShip   (floored at 0)
    Aggregated from the qtyInventoryTotals view per part+LG, the same source
    InventoryAvailability.htm and AvailableToBuild.htm use.

  FOUR DEFECTS IN THE .jrxml THAT THIS REPORT FIXES
    1. UOM CONVERSION WAS NEVER APPLIED. The .jrxml LEFT JOINs UOMCONVERSION
       but never references it, then divides available stock (held in the
       PART base UOM) by kititem.defaultQty (authored in the KIT LINE's UOM).
       demodb: "50ml Jar of Eye Cream" consumes 1.2 kg of Bulk Cream, whose
       part UOM is "20kg" -> the true figure is 0.06 base units per kit, so
       the .jrxml understates that line's capacity 20x. Same defect class as
       BillOfMaterials.jrxml / AvailableToBuild.jrxml.
    2. DISCOUNT AND TAX-RATE LINES WERE TREATED AS COMPONENTS. kititem
       .kitItemTypeId is ignored entirely, so a Discount (50) or Tax Rate (60)
       line — which has no product at all — is counted like a Standard one.
       Filtered to 10/20/30/40 here.
       The genuinely optional types ARE counted in the headline (see THE THREE
       FIGURES below), because the kit is configured with them; they are just
       broken out so the effect of dropping them is visible.
    3. "ALTERNATE PRODUCT" ROWS WERE TREATED AS COMPONENTS. kititem.kitTypeId
       20 = Alternate Product, not a kit line; the .jrxml counts them, and its
       COALESCE(NULLIF(defaultQty,0),1) turns their qty of 0 into 1, inventing
       a one-per-kit requirement. Filtered to kitTypeId = 10 here.
    4. OPTION GROUPS WERE SILENTLY DROPPED. A kit line whose productId is NULL
       (an option group, e.g. "Colour") is removed by the .jrxml's inner JOIN.
       Here the line resolves to its default kitoption choice, and the drill
       lists every alternative with its own availability.

  LOCATION-GROUP SCOPE — WHY THE FIGURES DIFFER FROM THE .jrxml
    The .jrxml has no LG scope at all: it sums every group's raw on-hand /
    allocated / not-available / drop-ship FIRST and floors the result ONCE.
    This report defaults to one row per kit x LG and floors each group.
    Those disagree whenever a group is OVER-ALLOCATED, because a negative group
    is netted against real stock elsewhere. demodb part 11857:

        Adelaide  9 on hand, 9 not available          ->   0
        Brisbane 18 on hand, 28 allocated             ->  -9   <-- over-allocated
        Melbourne 23 on hand                          -> +23
        company-wide sum                              ->  14

    So the Bearing Kit (2 x 11857) reads 7 company-wide but 11 in Melbourne.
    You cannot assemble a kit in Melbourne out of Brisbane's shortfall, so the
    per-LG figure is the actionable one — but the old report's is not wrong for
    the question it asks, and 60 part x LG rows in demodb are negative (38
    parts), so this is routine, not an edge case. The same netting is why the
    .jrxml shows Test Kit = 1: F201 is +40 in one group and -39 across four
    others.

    Filters > Scope switches to "Consolidated", which reproduces the .jrxml's
    arithmetic exactly for cross-checking (raw summed, floored once). Verified
    on demodb: Consolidated Kits Available matches the .jrxml on all 8 kits
    (14 / 7 / 0 / 0 / 1 / 1503 / 14 / 14). One residual gap — the .jrxml
    sums EVERY location group including inactive ones, while this report sums
    the groups the user selected (accessible + active).

  THE THREE FIGURES — two independent axes, made explicit
    A kit line can be optional, and a line can offer a CHOICE of products, so
    "how many can we do" has more than one honest answer. The report shows
    three, and the headline is deliberately the LEAST permissive:

      Kits Available   every line, DEFAULT option choice — the kit as it is
                       configured. The conservative number, and the one the
                       .jrxml computes.
      Excl. Optional   Optional + Variable-Optional lines left off the order.
                       Higher than the headline means an OPTIONAL line is the
                       thing holding the kit back.
      Best Variation   every line, BEST-STOCKED option choice. Higher than the
                       headline means the kit only needs a different option
                       picked.

    demodb "Test Kit", company-wide, is the case that makes this necessary:

      Frame (Optional)  F201 default -> 1 kit      F202 alternative -> 474
      H100  (Variable)  required                                   -> 123
      Colour (Var-Opt)  qty 0                                  unbounded

      Kits Available 1     as configured: the default frame allows one kit
      Excl. Optional 123   ship no frame at all; H100 then binds
      Best Variation 123   ship a frame, but F202; H100 still binds

    An earlier revision made the required-only figure the headline, which put
    123 in the Kits Available column while the kit as set up could supply one.
    That reads as though 123 are sellable. The headline is now the
    as-configured figure and the permissive ones have to earn attention.

  FEATURES
    - Kit summary table (FBLib.Table: sort / drag-reorder / drag-resize / lazy
      render / saved column layout). Filtering lives in the Filters drawer via
      FBLib.Common.MultiSelect (Location Group / Kit / Constraint Part) plus a
      kit-number search and availability chips.
    - Click ANY kit row to expand its per-line breakdown inline: qty per kit in
      the part's stocking UOM, on hand, available, kits supported, the limiting
      line(s) highlighted, optional lines marked, and every selectable
      alternative for an option line. An Expand all / Collapse all switcher in
      the header opens every row at once. Several kits can be open together, so
      two kits sharing a short component can be compared side by side.
    - "Excl. Optional" column shows what the kit would do with its optional
      lines left off, highlighted when that beats the headline.
    - "Best Variation" column — an optional / option-group line offers a CHOICE
      of products, so the kit has variations. This is the count with the
      best-stocked choice on every option line; when it beats Kits Available the
      kit is not blocked, it just needs a different option picked, and the panel
      names the swap. Computed by maximising each line independently (valid
      because MIN is monotone per line), so the combinations are never
      enumerated; a part reachable from two lines is flagged as contended
      because those lines would compete for the same stock. Per-variation
      figures are ALTERNATIVES, NOT ADDITIONS — variants share components.
    - The breakdown splits availability into On Hand / Committed / Not Available
      / Allocated / Available, because a line reading zero has three different
      possible causes and they call for different action:
        Not Available — in a QC-hold style location (countedAsAvailable = 0).
                        Physically present, unusable. demodb: Adelaide 11857.
        Committed     — reserved against a committed pick. demodb: Brisbane's
                        18, all of it.
        Allocated     — open order demand. NOT a physical state; the stock may
                        be sitting there pickable, just spoken for. Exceeding
                        On Hand means over-promised, which is what drives
                        Available negative. demodb: Brisbane 28 vs 18 on hand.
      Committed is display-only — the report's basis is Available for Sale,
      which nets out ALLOCATED, not committed. It comes from tag x location
      (qtyInventoryTotals has no committed column); the QTYCOMMITTED view is
      avoided because the qty views are TEMPTABLE and a WHERE does not push
      down. Not Available and Allocated are highlighted when they explain a zero.
    - "After Incoming" projects the count once open POs/MOs/TOs arrive.
    - CSV and real .xlsx export via FBLib.Export; print via the new-window
      workaround (window.print() is unreliable inside JxBrowser).

  DEPLOY ORDER (re-save on the server, in this order, or the report breaks):
    1. fb-styles  (Style  named exactly "fb-styles", source scripts/fb-styles.css)
    2. fb-lib     (Script named exactly "fb-lib",    source scripts/fb-lib.js)
    3. THIS report (the {% ... %} directives only re-run on save)

  STATUS: desk-built; the kit maths is validated against demodb. NOT yet
  client-tested - run it in the BI Script Editor before handing it over.
================================================================================
-->
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <!-- The page title IS the Fishbowl record name that tools/deploy derives
         (minus the " - Fishbowl BI" suffix), so it carries the section prefix
         the live picker sorts by. Plain hyphens, not em dashes — and do not
         write the tag name in this comment, the generator matches on it. -->
    <title>- Inventory - Kit Availability - Fishbowl BI</title>

    <!-- Inter font (matches the rest of the suite). -->
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700;800;900&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

    <!-- Shared Fishbowl BI lib — inlined by Fishbowl from the saved "fb-lib"
         script. Source of truth: scripts/fb-lib.js. -->
    <script>
        {% Script fb-lib %}
    </script>

    <!-- Shared Fishbowl BI stylesheet — inlined from the saved "fb-styles"
         Style (scripts/fb-styles.css). MUST come BEFORE the inline block so
         per-report rules win the cascade on identical selectors. -->
    <style>
        {% Style fb-styles %}
    </style>

    <style>
        /* =====================================================
           BASE + LAYOUT  (from Core_Dashboard_Template — tokens live in
           fb-styles; style new work off var(--…), never hardcoded hexes)
           ===================================================== */
        * { box-sizing: border-box; }
        html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; height: 100%; }
        body {
            font-family: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
            font-size: 13px; color: var(--c-primary); background: var(--bg-1);
            display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 100vh;
            padding-bottom: var(--debug-drawer-h, 0px);
            transition: padding-bottom 0.12s ease;
        }
        header h1 { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--c-primary); margin: 0; line-height: 1.15; }
        #statusLine { font-size: 12px; color: var(--c-tertiary); line-height: 1.15; margin: 2px 0 0; }
        .hdr-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }

        /* Drawer grid (from Core). */
        .fb-grid { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 14px 22px; align-items: flex-start; }
        .fb-group { flex: 1 1 220px; min-width: 220px; }
        .fb-grid-cols { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(210px, 1fr)); align-items: start; }
        .fb-grid-cols .fb-group { flex: none; min-width: 0; }
        .fb-grid-cols .fb-field select,
        .fb-grid-cols .fb-field input[type=text] { width: 100%; }
        @media (max-width: 520px) { .fb-grid-cols { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
        /* The Filters drawer hosts fb-lib multi-selects. The drawer body scrolls
           (overflow-y:auto), which CLIPS an open .ms-dropdown. The filter content
           is short and never needs to scroll, so let this drawer's body overflow
           visibly — the dropdown caps itself at 280px with its own scroll. */
        #filtersOverlay .fb-drawer-body { overflow: visible; }
        /* The drawer backdrop scrim is injected + managed by fb-lib
           (registerDrawer → #fbDrawerScrim). Never add a local scrim or a
           `.fb-drawer.open { z-index }` override: the drawer must keep the
           fb-styles z-index (10001) that sits above fb-lib's scrim (10000). */
        .fb-group-title {
            font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase;
            letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--c-secondary); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
            padding-bottom: 4px; margin-bottom: 8px;
        }
        .fb-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
        .fb-field label { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--c-secondary); }
        .fb-field select, .fb-field input[type=text] {
            padding: 4px 8px; font-size: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border);
            border-radius: 6px; background: var(--bg-1); font-family: inherit; color: #415157;
        }
        .fb-hint { font-size: 11px; color: var(--c-tertiary); margin: -2px 0 8px; line-height: 1.35; }

        /* Radio chips inside the filter drawer (availability + optional mode). */
        .fb-chips { display: flex; gap: 6px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
        .fb-chips label {
            display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; cursor: pointer;
            padding: 4px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-pill);
            font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--c-secondary); background: #fff;
        }
        .fb-chips input { display: none; }
        .fb-chips label.on { background: var(--tint-blue); border-color: var(--fb-blue); color: var(--fb-blue-accent); }

        .ds-btn { padding: 7px 13px; font-size: 12px; border-radius: 7px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); background: #fff; cursor: pointer; font-family: inherit; font-weight: 600; color: #415157; }
        .ds-btn:hover { background: var(--bg-2); }
        .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-primary); color: #fff; border-color: var(--color-primary); }
        .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-primary-dark); }
        .ds-btn-admin { background: var(--acc-orange-bg); border-color: var(--acc-orange); color: var(--acc-orange-con); margin-right: 6px; }
        .ds-lock-badge { background: var(--acc-orange-bg); color: var(--acc-orange-con); border: 1px solid var(--acc-orange); padding: 7px 10px; border-radius: 7px; font-size: 12px; margin-bottom: 14px; }

        /* App shell (from Core — no KPI strip). */
        .app-shell { width: 100%; margin: 0; padding: 0; flex: 1 1 auto; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0; }

        /* Data table (from Core — the styles FBLib.Table.init expects). Single
           sticky title row (32px); the per-column filter row is hidden, so the
           body scrolls directly under one sticky header with no gap. */
        .fb-table-container { flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; background: #fff; }
        table.fb-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 12px; table-layout: fixed; }
        table.fb-table th {
            background: var(--menu-bg); color: #fff; font-weight: 500;
            padding: 0 10px; height: 32px; text-align: left; white-space: nowrap;
            cursor: grab; user-select: none; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 10;
            overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
        }
        table.fb-table th:active { cursor: grabbing; }
        table.fb-table th:hover { background: #164A5F; }
        table.fb-table th.sort-asc::after  { content: ' \2191'; opacity: 0.8; }
        table.fb-table th.sort-desc::after { content: ' \2193'; opacity: 0.8; }
        table.fb-table th.col-drag-over { background: #164A5F; border-left: 3px solid #CBE5FB; }
        table.fb-table tr.filter-row { display: none; }
        /* Clip data to its own column — never bleed into the neighbour. */
        table.fb-table td {
            padding: 4px 10px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); white-space: nowrap;
            vertical-align: middle; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
        }
        /* Zebra striping is applied as a CLASS, not :nth-child — expanding a kit
           interleaves detail rows into the same tbody, which makes positional
           striping look random. _syncDetails() stamps .row-alt on every second
           SUMMARY row so the banding still counts kits, not DOM rows. */
        table.fb-table tr.row-alt > td { background: var(--bg-1); }
        table.fb-table tr.kit-row { cursor: pointer; }
        table.fb-table tr.kit-row:hover > td { background: var(--tint-blue) !important; }
        table.fb-table tr.kit-row.is-open > td { background: var(--tint-blue); box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 var(--fb-blue); }
        table.fb-table .num-cell { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
        .fb-row-link { color: var(--fb-blue); cursor: pointer; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 600; }
        .fb-row-link:hover { text-decoration: underline; color: var(--fb-blue-accent); }
        .fb-col-resize { position: absolute; right: 0; top: 0; width: 6px; height: 100%; cursor: col-resize; user-select: none; }
        .fb-col-resize:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.3); }

        /* Expander affordance in the Components / Constraint columns. These are
           NOT links any more — the whole kit row toggles — so they carry no
           click handler of their own and simply fall through to the row. */
        .drill-link { color: var(--fb-blue); cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; }
        table.fb-table tr.kit-row:hover .drill-link { text-decoration: underline; color: var(--fb-blue-accent); }
        .kit-chev { display: inline-block; width: 9px; margin-right: 3px; transition: transform 0.12s; }
        table.fb-table tr.is-open .kit-chev { transform: rotate(90deg); }

        /* Inline kit-line detail row. One full-width cell per expanded kit
           holding the breakdown table; the panel is inset so it reads as a
           child of the row above rather than as another grid row. */
        tr.kit-detail > td { padding: 0 !important; background: var(--bg-2) !important; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-strong); }
        .kit-detail-wrap { padding: 10px 14px 12px 26px; }

        /* ONE table, table-layout:fixed + a colgroup, so the numeric columns
           line up straight down the whole list including alternative rows. */
        /* max-width, not width:100% — on a wide panel the auto first column
           otherwise swallows every spare pixel and strands the numbers at the
           far right, yards from the part they belong to. */
        table.drill-tbl { width: 100%; max-width: 1140px; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 12px; table-layout: fixed; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--border); }
        /* Names the kit the panel belongs to — several can be open at once, and
           a panel scrolled away from its row is otherwise unattributable. */
        .kit-detail-title { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--c-primary); margin: 0 0 5px; }
        .kit-detail-title .lg { font-weight: 500; color: var(--c-secondary); }
        .kit-detail-title .qty { font-weight: 500; color: var(--c-secondary); }
        /* "This kit is not blocked, it just needs a different option picked." */
        .kit-best {
            font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--fb-success); background: var(--acc-sage);
            border: 1px solid #BBD6C6; border-radius: 6px;
            padding: 5px 9px; margin: 0 0 7px; display: inline-block;
        }
        .kit-best .muted { color: var(--c-secondary); font-weight: 400; }
        /* Best Variation grid cell, when a variation beats the kit as configured. */
        .best-up { color: var(--fb-success); font-weight: 700; cursor: help; }
        /* Excl. Optional, when dropping the optional lines would unblock the kit. */
        .excl-up { color: var(--acc-orange-con); font-weight: 700; cursor: help; }
        /* A component figure that EXPLAINS a zero — stock in a QC-hold location,
           or open demand exceeding what is on hand. */
        table.drill-tbl .avl-flag { color: var(--acc-orange-con); font-weight: 700; cursor: help; }
        /* A narrowed Location Group selection is remembered between sessions and
           is otherwise invisible — it silently changes every figure, and makes
           Consolidated disagree with the Jasper report. Call it out. */
        #statusLine .scope-warn { color: var(--acc-orange-con); cursor: help; }
        /* Per-option kit total + the winning pick, inside the breakdown. */
        table.drill-tbl .kit-if { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-weight: 400; font-size: 10.5px; cursor: help; }
        table.drill-tbl .best-pick {
            color: var(--fb-success); background: var(--acc-sage); border-radius: var(--r-pill);
            font-size: 9.5px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em;
            padding: 1px 5px; margin-left: 4px; cursor: help;
        }
        /* NOT sticky: these tables now sit inline inside the scrolling grid, so a
           sticky header would float over the rows above it. */
        /* SPECIFICITY: the grid's own `table.fb-table th/td` rules reach these
           nested cells too and outrank a bare `.drill-tbl th`, which rendered
           the breakdown header in the grid's dark sticky chrome and clipped
           every cell to one ellipsised line. Every selector below is therefore
           qualified `table.drill-tbl …` to match that weight and, coming later
           in the sheet, win. The sticky/grab/height chrome is reset explicitly. */
        table.drill-tbl th {
            background: var(--bg-2); color: var(--c-secondary); text-align: left;
            font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase;
            letter-spacing: 0.03em; padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
            position: static; height: auto; cursor: default; white-space: normal;
            overflow: visible; text-overflow: clip;
        }
        table.drill-tbl th.num { text-align: right; }
        /* These cells must beat the grid's own `table.fb-table td` rules, which
           would otherwise apply through the nesting and clip every line to one
           ellipsised row. */
        table.drill-tbl td {
            padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bg-2); vertical-align: top;
            white-space: normal; overflow: visible; text-overflow: clip;
        }
        table.drill-tbl td.num { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; }
        table.drill-tbl tr.constraint td { background: var(--acc-yellow-bg); }
        table.drill-tbl tr:hover > td { background: var(--tint-blue) !important; }
        table.drill-tbl tr.opt-row td { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent, transparent 7px, rgba(0,0,0,0.018) 7px, rgba(0,0,0,0.018) 14px); }
        table.drill-tbl tr.alt-row td { background: var(--bg-1); }
        table.drill-tbl td.comp-part { font-weight: 600; }
        table.drill-tbl td.comp-part > div { min-width: 0; }
        table.drill-tbl .comp-desc { color: var(--c-secondary); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 400; }
        table.drill-tbl .noninv { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-style: italic; }
        table.drill-tbl .line-type { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.03em; }
        /* Qty/Kit is shown in the PART's stocking UOM (see _drillRows); when the
           kit line was authored in a different unit the original rides along
           muted so the conversion is auditable rather than invisible. */
        table.drill-tbl .uom-orig { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 400; white-space: nowrap; cursor: help; }
        table.drill-tbl .uom-bad { color: var(--fb-negative); font-weight: 700; cursor: help; }
        .alt-toggle { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; cursor: pointer; color: var(--fb-blue); vertical-align: middle; margin-right: 2px; }
        .alt-toggle svg { width: 13px; height: 13px; transition: transform 0.12s; }
        .alt-toggle.open svg { transform: rotate(90deg); }
        .drill-hint { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--c-tertiary); margin: 0 0 7px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
        .drill-hint span.k { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; }
        .drill-hint .sw { display: inline-block; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--acc-yellow-bg); border: 1px solid var(--acc-yellow); }
        .drill-hint .sw-opt { display: inline-block; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 3px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent, transparent 3px, rgba(0,0,0,0.10) 3px, rgba(0,0,0,0.10) 6px); }

        /* Custom scrollbar (from Core). */
        .fb-drawer-body::-webkit-scrollbar, .fb-table-container::-webkit-scrollbar, .modal-body::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 8px; height: 8px; }
        .fb-drawer-body::-webkit-scrollbar-track, .fb-table-container::-webkit-scrollbar-track, .modal-body::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: var(--bg-2); border-radius: 4px; }
        .fb-drawer-body::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb, .fb-table-container::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb, .modal-body::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--border-strong); border-radius: 4px; }

        @media print {
            html, body { overflow: visible; }
            @page { size: A4 landscape; margin: 0.5in; }
            header, .hdr-btn, .fb-drawer, .fblib-debug-drawer { display: none !important; }
            /* Printing goes through printReport()'s own window, but if the
               browser prints this page directly, expanded panels should not be
               sliced across a page break. */
            tr.kit-detail { break-inside: avoid; }
            .fb-table-container { overflow: visible !important; }
            table.fb-table th { position: static !important; background: #ddd !important; color: #000 !important; }
        }
    </style>
</head>

<!-- ==================== HELP DRAWER ==================== -->
<div id="helpOverlay" class="fb-drawer">
    <div class="fb-drawer-head">
        <h2>📖 How to Use This Report</h2>
        <button type="button" class="fb-drawer-close" onclick="FBLib.Common.closeDrawer('helpOverlay')" aria-label="Close">×</button>
    </div>
    <div class="fb-drawer-body">
        <div class="fb-grid">
            <div class="fb-group" style="flex:1 1 320px;">
                <div class="fb-group-title">What it shows</div>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;">One row per <strong>kit product × location group</strong>. <strong>Kits Available</strong> is how many complete kits you could assemble and sell right now from stock in that location group, <em>as the kit is configured</em> — capped by the scarcest kit line (the <strong>constraint part</strong>).</p>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;">"Available" means <strong>Available for Sale</strong> = On Hand − Allocated − Not Available + Drop Ship, the same basis as Fishbowl's Inventory Availability and Available to Build reports.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="fb-group" style="flex:1 1 320px;">
                <div class="fb-group-title">The three figures</div>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;"><strong>Kits Available</strong> is the kit <em>exactly as it is configured</em> — every line, each at its default option choice. It is the conservative figure and the one that matches Fishbowl's own Kit Availability report.</p>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;">The other two are the ways of beating it. <strong>Excl. Optional</strong> drops the Optional and Variable-Optional lines, which an order does not include unless the salesperson picks them — when it is higher, an optional line is what is holding the kit back. <strong>Best Variation</strong> keeps every line but takes the best-stocked choice on each.</p>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;">Discount and Tax Rate lines are never components and are always ignored.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="fb-group" style="flex:1 1 320px;">
                <div class="fb-group-title">Variations</div>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;">An optional or option-group line lets the salesperson pick from several products, so the kit has <strong>variations</strong>. <strong>Best Variation</strong> is how many you could make with the best-stocked choice on every option line — when it beats <strong>Kits Available</strong>, the kit isn't really blocked, it just needs a different option picked, and the expanded panel names which one.</p>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;">Inside the panel each option shows its own stock <em>and</em> the kit total it would produce. These totals are <strong>alternatives, not additions</strong> — two variations of the same kit draw on the same shared components, so you cannot make the best of both.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="fb-group" style="flex:1 1 320px;">
                <div class="fb-group-title">Drill & columns</div>
                <ul style="font-size:12px; color:#415157; padding-left:18px; margin:4px 0;">
                    <li><strong>Click any row</strong> to expand its kit lines underneath: each line's available stock and how many kits it supports, with the limiting line(s) highlighted. Click again to collapse. <strong>Expand all</strong> in the header opens every row at once.</li>
                    <li><strong>Qty / Kit</strong> is shown in the part's stocking UOM; where the kit line was authored in another unit, the original is in brackets.</li>
                    <li>An <strong>option line</strong> expands (▸) to list every selectable alternative with its own availability — useful when the default choice is the bottleneck.</li>
                    <li><strong>After Incoming</strong> projects the count once open POs/MOs/TOs land.</li>
                    <li><strong>Sort</strong> by clicking a header; <strong>reorder</strong> by dragging headers; <strong>resize</strong> by dragging a header edge. Your layout is saved.</li>
                </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="fb-group" style="flex:1 1 320px;">
                <div class="fb-group-title">Filters & export</div>
                <p style="font-size:12px; color:#415157;">By default only kits you can <strong>build now</strong> are listed — switch to <strong>All kits</strong> or <strong>Zero-available</strong> in the filter drawer, where you can also multi-select <strong>Location Group</strong>, <strong>Kit Product</strong> and <strong>Constraint Part</strong>, and search a kit number. <strong>CSV</strong> and <strong>Excel</strong> export exactly the rows on screen; <strong>Print</strong> opens a print-formatted window.</p>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

<script>

}

// ============================================================================
//  FB-LIB FEATURE CHECK
// ============================================================================
(function () {
    var missing = [];
    if (!window.FBLib) missing.push('window.FBLib');
    if (window.FBLib && !FBLib.Common) missing.push('FBLib.Common');

    function showBanner() {

            missing.join('</code>, <code style="background:#fff;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:3px;">') +
            '</code>. Open BI Script Editor, confirm a script named exactly <code>fb-lib</code> exists with the current contents of <code>scripts/fb-lib.js</code>, then re-save THIS report.';
        document.body.appendChild(banner);
        try { console.error('[KitAvailability] fb-lib feature check failed:', missing); } catch (_) {}
    }
    if (document.body) showBanner(); else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', showBanner);
})();

// ============================================================================
//  FBLIB SETTINGS INIT
// ============================================================================
try {
    FBLib.Settings.init({
        masterStorage: 'userProperties',   // shared admin defaults via userproperties, not report data (which needs a SAVED report — see FBLib.SharedData)
        userKey:   'cdx.bi.kitavailability.user.v1',
        masterKey: 'cdx.bi.kitavailability.master.v1',
        defaults: {
            v: 1,
            rememberFilters: true,
            showDebug: false,
            lgSel: [],               // remembered LG selection (empty = all accessible)
            availFilter: 'now',      // 'all' | 'now' | 'zero'
            scopeMode: 'perlg',      // 'perlg' | 'consolidated' (the .jrxml's company-wide roll-up)
            tablePrefs: null         // FBLib.Table column order/widths/sort
        },
        propFallback: {
            showDebug: { name: 'BI_SHOW_DEBUG', dflt: 'false', parse: function (v) { return v === 'true'; } }
        }
    });
} catch (e) { console.warn('FBLib.Settings.init failed:', e); }

var _resolve = function (key, dflt) {
    try { var v = FBLib.Settings.resolve(key); return (v === undefined || v === null) ? dflt : v; }
    catch (_) { return dflt; }
};
var _setUserKey = function (key, value) {
    try { FBLib.Settings.setUserKey(key, value); FBLib.Settings.saveUser(); } catch (_) {}
};
var debugLog = function (msg, kind) { FBLib.Common.debugLog(msg, kind); };

// ============================================================================
//  KIT LINE TYPES  (kititem.kitItemTypeId — verified against kititemtype)
// ============================================================================
//   10 Standard           — always on the order. Constrains.
//   20 Optional           — only if the salesperson adds it. Optional.
//   30 Variable           — always on the order, qty may be changed. Constrains.
//   40 Variable-Optional  — optional AND variable-qty. Optional.
//   50 Discount           — a discount line, no product. Never a component.
//   60 Tax Rate           — a tax line, no product. Never a component.
// kititem.kitTypeId is a DIFFERENT lookup: 10 = Kit Item, 20 = Alternate
// Product. Only kitTypeId 10 rows are kit lines; type 20 rows are alternates
// hanging off a product and must not be treated as requirements.
var LINE_REQUIRED = [10, 30];
var LINE_OPTIONAL = [20, 40];
var LINE_COMPONENT = LINE_REQUIRED.concat(LINE_OPTIONAL);   // 50/60 excluded entirely

// ============================================================================
//  STATE
// ============================================================================
var _allRows = [];            // every summary row (kit x LG) in the current scope
var _dataset = [];            // _allRows after the client filters (fed to the table)
var _linesByKit = {};         // kitproductid -> [kit line objects]
var _optionsByLine = {};      // kititemid -> [alternative option objects]
var _kitMetaById = {};        // kitproductid -> { kitnum, kitdesc }
var _availMap = {};           // "partid|lgid" -> { available, onhand, onorder }
var _constraintByKey = {};    // "kitproductid|lgid" -> Set(partid) of limiting lines
var _bestByKey = {};          // "kitproductid|lgid" -> computeKitBest() result
var _table = null;
var _lgMs = null;             // Location Group multi-select (drives the queries)
var _kitMs = null;            // Kit multi-select (client-side filter)
var _constraintMs = null;     // Constraint Part multi-select (client-side filter)
var _lgAccessible = [];       // [{id,name}] the user can access
var _loadToken = 0;
var _availFilter = 'now';
var _scopeMode = 'perlg';     // 'perlg' | 'consolidated'

// Pseudo location group for Consolidated scope. Availability is summed across
// the selected groups as RAW (unfloored) figures and floored ONCE at the end —
// see the consolidation pass in loadDashboard for why that matters.
var LG_ALL = 'ALL';

var CAP_KITS = 3000;          // safety cap on the kit-header query

// ============================================================================
//  RUNQUERY NORMALISER
// ============================================================================
async function runQueryP(sql) {
    if (typeof runQueryAsync === 'function') {
        var r = await runQueryAsync(sql);
        return Array.isArray(r) ? r : [];
    }
    var raw = runQuery(sql);
    if (!raw) return [];
    try { var p = JSON.parse(raw); return Array.isArray(p) ? p : []; } catch (_) { return []; }
}

function escSQL(s) { return FBLib.Common.escSQL(s); }
function num(v) { var n = parseFloat(v); return isNaN(n) ? 0 : n; }
function intList(arr) {
    return (arr || []).map(function (x) { return parseInt(x, 10); })
        .filter(function (n) { return !isNaN(n); });
}
function fmtQty(v) { return FBLib.Common.formatQty(v); }
function fmtMoney(v) { return FBLib.Common.formatMoney(v); }
function esc(s) { return String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, function (c) { return ({ '&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"',"'":''' })[c]; }); }
// MySQL bit(1) comes back as a raw byte, so `flag + 0` is selected in SQL and
// this only has to cope with 1 / '1' / true.
function truthy(v) { return v === true || v === 1 || v === '1'; }

// The location groups currently in scope: the user's selection, else every
// accessible LG. Availability is computed per LG within this set.
function selectedLgIds() {
    var sel = _lgMs ? intList(_lgMs.getSelected()) : [];
    if (sel.length) return sel;
    return _lgAccessible.map(function (l) { return parseInt(l.id, 10); }).filter(function (n) { return !isNaN(n); });
}
function lgNameById(id) {
    if (String(id) === LG_ALL) {
        var n = selectedLgIds().length;
        return 'All selected (' + n + ' LG' + (n === 1 ? '' : 's') + ')';
    }
    var m = _lgAccessible.find(function (l) { return String(l.id) === String(id); });
    return m ? m.name : ('LG ' + id);
}
// The groups the consolidated figure actually rolls up, for tooltips + exports.
function selectedLgNames() { return selectedLgIds().map(lgNameById).join(', '); }

// ============================================================================

function _qtyCell(v) { return (v == null || v === '') ? '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)">—</span>' : fmtQty(num(v)); }
// Plain figures in the grid — no pills. Zero reads as muted, available as bold.
function _availCell(v) {
    if (v == null || v === '') return '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)">—</span>';
    var n = num(v);

        ? '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)">0</span>'

}
// "Excl. Optional" — the kit with its Optional / Variable-Optional lines left
// off the order entirely. Higher than the headline means an OPTIONAL line is
// what is holding the kit back, and simply not shipping it unblocks you; that
// is worth calling out, so it is the only case that gets colour.
function _exclOptCell(v, row) {
    if (v == null || v === '') return '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)">—</span>';
    var n = num(v), base = num(row.qtyavailable);
    if (n <= base) {
        return '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)" title="' +
            esc('No optional line is limiting this kit — dropping the optional lines would not help.') +
            '">' + fmtQty(n) + '</span>';
    }
    var names = (row._optCapping || []).join(', ');
    return '<span class="excl-up" title="' +
        esc('Optional line(s) ' + (names || '—') + ' cap this kit at ' + fmtQty(base) + '. Leave them off ' +
            'the order and you could supply ' + fmtQty(n) + '. An Optional line is not added unless the ' +
            'salesperson picks it, so this is often the realistic figure.') +
        '">' + fmtQty(n) + '</span>';
}
// "Best Variation" — the same every-line basis as the headline, but with the
// best-stocked choice on each option line, so the two are directly comparable.
// Called out in green only when it beats the kit as configured, because that is
// the actionable case: the kit is not really blocked, it just needs a different
// option picked.
function _bestCell(v, row) {
    if (v == null || v === '') return '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)">—</span>';
    var n = num(v), def = num(row.qtyavailable);
    var caveat = row._bestContended
        ? ' Note: two lines on this kit can select the same part, so they would compete for the same stock — treat this as an upper bound.'
        : '';
    if (n > def) {
        var swaps = (row._bestSwaps || []);
        var tip = (swaps.length ? 'Choose ' + swaps.join('; ') + ' — that lifts this kit from ' + fmtQty(def) + ' to ' + fmtQty(n) + '.'
                                : 'A different option choice lifts this kit from ' + fmtQty(def) + ' to ' + fmtQty(n) + '.') +
                  ' Click the row for the full breakdown.';
        return '<span class="best-up" title="' + esc(tip + caveat) + '">' + fmtQty(n) + '</span>';
    }
    return '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)" title="' +
        esc('No alternative option improves on the kit as configured.' + caveat) + '">' + fmtQty(n) + '</span>';
}
// Location Group cell. Consolidated scope shows one pseudo group, so name the

// Components cell — the row's expander affordance. The chevron is rotated by

function clearFilters() {
    document.getElementById('filterKit').value = '';
    document.getElementById('filterActiveOnly').checked = true;
    _setAvailFilter('now');
    _setUserKey('availFilter', 'now');
    _setScopeMode('perlg');
    _setUserKey('scopeMode', 'perlg');
    if (_lgMs) _lgMs.setSelected([]);
    if (_kitMs) _kitMs.setSelected([]);
    if (_constraintMs) _constraintMs.setSelected([]);
    loadDashboard();
}

async function loadFilters() {
    // Location groups the current user can access (getLocationGroupList), active only.
    try {
        var ids = (typeof getLocationGroupList === 'function' ? getLocationGroupList() : []) || [];
        var where = ids.length ? (' AND id IN (' + intList(ids).join(',') + ')') : '';
        var lgs = await runQueryP('SELECT id, name FROM locationgroup WHERE activeflag = 1' + where + ' ORDER BY name');
        _lgAccessible = lgs.map(function (r) { return { id: parseInt(r.id, 10), name: r.name || ('LG ' + r.id) }; });
        _lgMs.setItems(_lgAccessible.map(function (l) { return { value: l.id, label: l.name }; }));
        // Restore the remembered LG selection only when "Remember filter
        // selections" is on; otherwise every session starts on all-accessible.
        var savedLg = _resolve('lgSel', []);
        if (_resolve('rememberFilters', true) && Array.isArray(savedLg) && savedLg.length) _lgMs.setSelected(savedLg);
    } catch (e) { debugLog('loadFilters: locationgroup failed: ' + e.message, 'warn'); }
}

// ============================================================================
//  CLIENT-SIDE FILTERS  (availability chip + Kit / Constraint multi-selects).
//  Applied over _allRows -> _dataset with no re-query, so toggling them
//  repaints instantly.
// ============================================================================
function _setAvailFilter(v) {
    _availFilter = (v === 'now' || v === 'zero') ? v : 'all';
    document.querySelectorAll('#availChips label').forEach(function (el) {
        el.classList.toggle('on', el.getAttribute('data-v') === _availFilter);
        var input = el.querySelector('input'); if (input) input.checked = (el.getAttribute('data-v') === _availFilter);
    });
}
function onAvailFilterChange(v) {
    _setAvailFilter(v);
    _setUserKey('availFilter', _availFilter);
    _refreshTable();
}
function _setScopeMode(v) {
    _scopeMode = (v === 'consolidated') ? 'consolidated' : 'perlg';
    document.querySelectorAll('#scopeChips label').forEach(function (el) {
        el.classList.toggle('on', el.getAttribute('data-v') === _scopeMode);
        var input = el.querySelector('input'); if (input) input.checked = (el.getAttribute('data-v') === _scopeMode);
    });
}
// Scope only changes which LG key the rows are built on, and both the per-group
// and the consolidated availability are already in _availMap — so this is a
// recompute, not a re-query. Expansion keys embed the LG, so they are dropped.
function onScopeModeChange(v) {
    _setScopeMode(v);
    _setUserKey('scopeMode', _scopeMode);
    _expanded.clear();
    _rebuildRows();
    _populateValueFilters();
    _refreshTable();
}
function _applyClientFilters() {
    var kitSel = _kitMs ? new Set(_kitMs.getSelected().map(String)) : new Set();
    var conSel = _constraintMs ? new Set(_constraintMs.getSelected().map(String)) : new Set();
    _dataset = _allRows.filter(function (r) {
        if (_availFilter === 'now'  && !(num(r.qtyavailable) >= 1)) return false;
        if (_availFilter === 'zero' && !(r.qtyavailable != null && num(r.qtyavailable) === 0)) return false;
        if (kitSel.size && !kitSel.has(String(r.kitnum))) return false;
        if (conSel.size && !(r._constraintParts || []).some(function (p) { return conSel.has(String(p)); })) return false;
        return true;
    });
}
// Re-apply the client filters + repaint (no re-query). Rows that drop out of
// the filter keep their expanded state in _expanded, so they come back open if
// the filter is widened again — the reconciler only paints what is on screen.
function _refreshTable() {
    _applyClientFilters();
    if (_table) _table.render();
    _syncDetails();
    document.getElementById('statusLine').innerHTML = _statusText();
}
// Populate the Kit + Constraint multi-selects from the loaded rows, preserving
// any still-valid current selection.
function _populateValueFilters() {
    var kits = {}, cons = {};
    _allRows.forEach(function (r) {
        if (r.kitnum) kits[r.kitnum] = true;
        (r._constraintParts || []).forEach(function (p) { if (p) cons[p] = true; });
    });
    if (_kitMs) {
        var keepKit = _kitMs.getSelected().filter(function (v) { return kits[v]; });
        _kitMs.setItems(Object.keys(kits).sort().map(function (v) { return { value: v, label: v }; }));
        _kitMs.setSelected(keepKit);
    }
    if (_constraintMs) {
        var keepCon = _constraintMs.getSelected().filter(function (v) { return cons[v]; });
        _constraintMs.setItems(Object.keys(cons).sort().map(function (v) { return { value: v, label: v }; }));
        _constraintMs.setSelected(keepCon);
    }
}
// The status line has to answer two questions people actually hit:
//   "why am I only seeing one location group?"  -> rows hidden by the
//      availability chip, which defaults to Available-now and silently drops
//      every zero row (a kit stocked in one group shows exactly one row).
//   "why doesn't Consolidated match the Jasper report?" -> because it rolls up
//      only the groups IN SCOPE, and the LG selection is remembered between
//      sessions. Consolidating one group just returns that group.
// Both are reported, and a narrowed LG scope is called out, because neither is
// visible anywhere else on screen. Returns HTML.
function _statusText() {
    var cons = (_scopeMode === 'consolidated');
    var inScope = selectedLgIds().length, accessible = _lgAccessible.length;
    var bits = [
        _dataset.length.toLocaleString() + ' of ' + _allRows.length.toLocaleString() +
            (cons ? ' kit' : ' kit×LG') + ' row' + (_allRows.length === 1 ? '' : 's')
    ];
    var hidden = _allRows.length - _dataset.length;
    if (hidden > 0) {
        var why = (_availFilter === 'now') ? 'Available now'
                : (_availFilter === 'zero') ? 'Zero-available' : 'the filters';
        bits.push(hidden.toLocaleString() + ' hidden by ' + why);
    }
    // Always state the roll-up width in Consolidated — it defines the figure.
    // In per-LG only mention it when narrowed, so the common case stays quiet.
    if (cons || inScope < accessible) {
        var lgTxt = (cons ? 'consolidated across ' : '') + inScope + ' of ' + accessible +
                    ' location group' + (accessible === 1 ? '' : 's');
        bits.push(inScope < accessible
            ? '<strong class="scope-warn" title="' + esc('Only ' + inScope + ' of your ' + accessible +
                ' location groups are selected, so every figure covers just those. Clear the Location ' +
                'Group filter to include them all.') + '">⚠ ' + esc(lgTxt) + '</strong>'
            : esc(lgTxt));
    }
    return bits.join(' · ');
}

//  SQL BUILDERS
// ============================================================================
// Kit products (product.kitFlag = 1). Kit products carry no partId of their own
// — a kit is assembled at pick time, never stocked — so there is no finished-
// good availability column here, unlike AvailableToBuild.
function buildKitHeaderSQL() {
    var where = ['p.kitFlag = 1'];
    if (document.getElementById('filterActiveOnly').checked) where.push('p.activeFlag = 1');
    var kit = document.getElementById('filterKit').value.trim();
    if (kit) where.push("p.num LIKE '%" + escSQL(kit) + "%'");
    return [
        'SELECT p.id AS kitproductid, p.num AS kitnum, p.description AS kitdesc,',
        '       COALESCE(p.price, 0) AS kitprice, u.code AS kituom',
        'FROM product p',
        'LEFT JOIN uom u ON u.id = p.uomId',
        'WHERE ' + where.join(' AND '),
        'ORDER BY p.num',
        'LIMIT ' + (CAP_KITS + 1)
    ].join('\n');
}

// Kit lines for a set of kit products.
//   - kitTypeId = 10 keeps genuine kit lines and drops "Alternate Product"
//     rows (kitTypeId 20), which are not requirements.
//   - kitItemTypeId IN (10,20,30,40) drops Discount (50) and Tax Rate (60).
//   - A line with no productId is an OPTION GROUP; it resolves to the default
//     kitoption choice so the group still contributes its default component
//     (the .jrxml's inner JOIN dropped these lines entirely).
//   - The uomconversion factors ride along so qty-per-kit normalises to the
//     part base UOM in JS. `convok` records whether a conversion actually
//     exists, so a silent 1:1 fallback can be flagged rather than trusted.
function buildKitLineSQL(kitIds) {
    return [
        'SELECT ki.kitProductId AS kitproductid, ki.id AS kititemid, ki.sortOrder AS sortorder,',
        '       ki.kitItemTypeId AS linetypeid, kitype.name AS linetype,',
        '       COALESCE(ki.defaultQty, 0) AS kitqty,',
        '       COALESCE(ki.description, \'\') AS linedesc,',
        '       (ki.productId IS NULL) AS isoptiongroup,',
        '       cp.id AS productid, cp.num AS productnum,',
        '       part.id AS partid, part.num AS partnum, part.description AS partdesc,',
        '       part.typeId AS parttype, partuom.code AS partuom, kiuom.code AS kituom,',
        '       (ki.uomId = part.uomId OR uc.multiply IS NOT NULL) AS convok,',
        '       COALESCE(uc.multiply, 1) AS multiply, COALESCE(uc.factor, 1) AS factor',
        'FROM kititem ki',
        'JOIN kititemtype kitype ON kitype.id = ki.kitItemTypeId',
        // Default choice for an option group. defaultFlag is bit(1); comparing
        // to 1 works server-side (only the SELECTed value needs a +0).
        'LEFT JOIN kitoption kodef ON kodef.kitItemId = ki.id AND kodef.defaultFlag = 1',
        'LEFT JOIN product cp ON cp.id = COALESCE(ki.productId, kodef.productId)',
        'LEFT JOIN part ON part.id = cp.partId',
        'LEFT JOIN uom partuom ON partuom.id = part.uomId',
        'LEFT JOIN uom kiuom ON kiuom.id = ki.uomId',
        'LEFT JOIN uomconversion uc ON uc.fromUomId = ki.uomId AND uc.toUomId = part.uomId',
        'WHERE ki.kitTypeId = 10',
        '  AND ki.kitItemTypeId IN (' + LINE_COMPONENT.join(',') + ')',
        '  AND ki.kitProductId IN (' + kitIds.join(',') + ')',
        'ORDER BY ki.kitProductId, ki.sortOrder, ki.id'
    ].join('\n');
}

// Selectable alternatives for the given kit lines (the drill's expand rows).
function buildKitOptionSQL(lineIds) {
    return [
        'SELECT ko.kitItemId AS kititemid, (ko.defaultFlag + 0) AS isdefault,',
        '       p.id AS productid, p.num AS productnum,',
        '       part.id AS partid, part.num AS partnum, part.description AS partdesc,',
        '       part.typeId AS parttype, partuom.code AS partuom',
        'FROM kitoption ko',
        'JOIN product p ON p.id = ko.productId',
        'LEFT JOIN part ON part.id = p.partId',
        'LEFT JOIN uom partuom ON partuom.id = part.uomId',
        'WHERE ko.kitItemId IN (' + lineIds.join(',') + ')',
        'ORDER BY ko.kitItemId, ko.defaultFlag DESC, p.num'
    ].join('\n');
}

// Committed per part+LG. NOT in qtyInventoryTotals — that view has no committed
// column — so it comes from tag x location, which is also the definition the
// QTYCOMMITTED view uses (no tag-type and no location-type filter). Queried
// inline rather than through the view because the qty views are TEMPTABLE: a
// WHERE does not push down, so filtering the view would still materialise every
// part. `tag.partId` is indexed, so this form is the cheap one.
//
// Committed is shown in the breakdown ONLY. It is deliberately NOT part of the
// headline figure: this report's basis is Available for Sale, which nets out
// ALLOCATED (open demand). Committed is the different, physical measure — stock
// actually reserved on a committed pick — and it is in the panel so that a line
// reading zero says WHICH of the three reasons applies.
function buildCommittedSQL(partIds, lgIds) {
    return [
        'SELECT t.partId AS partid, l.locationGroupId AS lgid,',
        '       COALESCE(SUM(t.qtyCommitted), 0) AS committed',
        'FROM tag t',
        'JOIN location l ON l.id = t.locationId',
        'WHERE t.partId IN (' + partIds.join(',') + ')',
        '  AND l.locationGroupId IN (' + lgIds.join(',') + ')',
        'GROUP BY t.partId, l.locationGroupId'
    ].join('\n');
}

// Available-for-Sale per part+LG, from qtyInventoryTotals (same source as
// InventoryAvailability.htm / AvailableToBuild.htm). Scoped by LG + part set.
function buildAvailabilitySQL(partIds, lgIds) {
    return [
        'SELECT partId AS partid, locationGroupId AS lgid,',
        '       SUM(qtyOnHand)       AS onhand,',
        '       SUM(qtyNotAvailable) AS notavail,',
        '       SUM(qtyDropship)     AS dropship,',
        '       SUM(qtyAllocated)    AS allocated,',
        '       SUM(qtyOnOrder)      AS onorder',
        'FROM qtyInventoryTotals',
        'WHERE locationGroupId IN (' + lgIds.join(',') + ') AND partId IN (' + partIds.join(',') + ')',
        'GROUP BY partId, locationGroupId'
    ].join('\n');
}

// ============================================================================
//  COMPUTE HELPERS
// ============================================================================
// A line only constrains a kit when all of these hold:
//   * it resolved to an INVENTORY part (typeId 10). Service / Labour / Overhead
//     / Non-Inventory lines have no stock to run out of.
//   * it consumes a positive quantity. A zero-qty line takes nothing, so it can
//     never be the bottleneck. (The .jrxml coerced qty 0 to 1, inventing a
//     requirement that does not exist.)
//   * its line type is in scope for the current optional basis.
function _lineIsInventory(l) { return l.parttype === 10 && l.partid > 0; }
function _lineQtyPerKit(l) { return l.kitqty * (l.multiply / l.factor); }
function _lineConstrains(l, includeOptional) {
    if (!_lineIsInventory(l)) return false;
    if (!(_lineQtyPerKit(l) > 0)) return false;
    if (includeOptional) return LINE_COMPONENT.indexOf(l.linetypeid) !== -1;
    return LINE_REQUIRED.indexOf(l.linetypeid) !== -1;
}
function availGet(pid, lg, projected) {
    var a = _availMap[pid + '|' + lg];
    if (!a) return 0;
    return projected ? (a.available + a.onorder) : a.available;
}
// Kits supported by one kit x LG, over the lines in scope.
//   { qty, constraint: [{partid, partnum, kits}] }
// qty is null when no line can constrain the kit at all (nothing to divide) —
// rendered as an em dash, never as zero, because "no inventory line" and "no
// stock" are different answers.
function computeKit(kitId, lg, includeOptional, projected) {
    var lines = _linesByKit[kitId] || [];
    var scoped = lines.filter(function (l) { return _lineConstrains(l, includeOptional); });
    if (!scoped.length) return { qty: null, constraint: [] };
    var minKits = Infinity, per = [];
    scoped.forEach(function (l) {
        var qpk = _lineQtyPerKit(l);
        var avail = availGet(l.partid, lg, projected);
        var kits = Math.floor(avail / qpk);
        per.push({ partid: l.partid, partnum: l.partnum, kits: kits });
        if (kits < minKits) minKits = kits;
    });
    if (!isFinite(minKits)) return { qty: null, constraint: [] };
    return {
        qty: Math.max(0, minKits),
        constraint: per.filter(function (p) { return p.kits === minKits; })
    };
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  VARIATIONS — a kit line can offer a CHOICE of products
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An Optional or option-group line resolves to one default product but the
// salesperson may pick any of its `kitoption` alternatives instead, so the kit
// has variations. demodb "Test Kit" in Adelaide is the case that matters: the
// default Frame F201 has 0 available, which drags the whole configured kit to
// 0, while the alternative F202 has 323 — pick that and the kit runs to 69
// (capped by the required H100). The headline figure alone hides that entirely.
//
// Every product a line could resolve to: its own default first, then each
// selectable kitoption not already listed.
function _lineChoices(l) {
    var out = [], seen = {};
    if (l.partid) {
        out.push({ partid: l.partid, partnum: l.partnum, partdesc: l.partdesc,
                   parttype: l.parttype, partuom: l.partuom, isdefault: true });
        seen[l.partid] = true;
    }
    (_optionsByLine[l.kititemid] || []).forEach(function (o) {
        if (!o.partid || seen[o.partid]) return;
        seen[o.partid] = true;
        out.push({ partid: o.partid, partnum: o.partnum, partdesc: o.partdesc,
                   parttype: o.parttype, partuom: o.partuom, isdefault: !l.partid && o.isdefault });
    });
    return out;
}
// Kits one CHOICE supports. Infinity means "cannot constrain" — a non-inventory
// part, or a line that consumes nothing — so it drops out of the MIN.
function _choiceKits(choice, qpk, lg, projected) {
    if (!(qpk > 0)) return Infinity;
    if (!choice || !choice.partid || choice.parttype !== 10) return Infinity;
    return Math.floor(availGet(choice.partid, lg, projected) / qpk);
}
// The best a single line can do, and which choice gets there.
function _lineBest(l, lg, projected) {
    var qpk = _lineQtyPerKit(l);
    var scored = _lineChoices(l).map(function (c) {
        return { choice: c, kits: _choiceKits(c, qpk, lg, projected) };
    });
    if (!scored.length) return { kits: Infinity, choice: null, scored: [] };
    var top = scored.reduce(function (a, b) { return b.kits > a.kits ? b : a; });
    return { kits: top.kits, choice: top.choice, scored: scored };
}
// The ceiling for a kit you actually configure and sell: EVERY line counted
// (optional included, because a variation is a kit someone orders), each set to
// its best-stocked choice.
//
// Maximising each line INDEPENDENTLY is valid rather than a shortcut: MIN is
// monotone in each line, so max-over-configurations of the min equals the min
// of each line's max. No need to enumerate the combinations (Test Kit alone has
// 2 x 3 = 6, and that product grows with every option).
//
// It holds only while no part is reachable from two different lines. When one
// is, those lines would compete for the same stock and the independent maximum
// overstates — `contended` records that so the cell can say so rather than
// quietly report a number nobody can hit.
function computeKitBest(kitId, lg, projected) {
    var lines = (_linesByKit[kitId] || []).filter(function (l) {
        return LINE_COMPONENT.indexOf(l.linetypeid) !== -1;
    });
    if (!lines.length) return { qty: null, picks: [], swaps: [], contended: false };
    var minKits = Infinity, picks = [], swaps = [], seenPart = {}, contended = false;
    lines.forEach(function (l) {
        var b = _lineBest(l, lg, projected);
        _lineChoices(l).forEach(function (c) {
            if (seenPart[c.partid]) contended = true;
            seenPart[c.partid] = true;
        });
        picks.push({ line: l, best: b });
        // A swap worth naming: this line has a choice, and the winner is not
        // the product the kit defaults to.
        if (b.choice && !b.choice.isdefault && _lineChoices(l).length > 1) {
            swaps.push((l.linedesc || l.partnum || 'line') + ' = ' + b.choice.partnum);
        }
        if (b.kits < minKits) minKits = b.kits;
    });
    if (!isFinite(minKits)) return { qty: null, picks: picks, swaps: swaps, contended: contended };
    return { qty: Math.max(0, minKits), picks: picks, swaps: swaps, contended: contended };
}
// What the kit totals if this line is committed to this choice and every other
// line takes its own best. Used in the panel so each alternative shows not just
// what the PART supports but what the KIT would come to.
function _kitTotalIfChosen(kitId, lgId, line, choice) {
    var mine = _choiceKits(choice, _lineQtyPerKit(line), lgId, false);
    var others = Infinity;
    (_linesByKit[kitId] || []).forEach(function (o) {
        if (o.kititemid === line.kititemid) return;
        if (LINE_COMPONENT.indexOf(o.linetypeid) === -1) return;
        var k = _lineBest(o, lgId, false).kits;
        if (k < others) others = k;
    });
    var v = Math.min(mine, others);
    return isFinite(v) ? Math.max(0, v) : null;
}

// Rebuild _allRows from the already-loaded lines + availability. Split out of
// loadDashboard so the optional-basis toggle repaints without re-querying.
function _rebuildRows() {
    // Consolidated scope collapses to ONE pseudo group whose availability was
    // rolled up (raw, floored once) in loadDashboard — so everything downstream,
    // including the drill, works through the same _availMap lookups.
    var lgIds = (_scopeMode === 'consolidated') ? [LG_ALL] : selectedLgIds();
    _allRows = [];
    _constraintByKey = {};
    _bestByKey = {};
    Object.keys(_linesByKit).forEach(function (k) {
        var kitId = parseInt(k, 10);
        var meta = _kitMetaById[kitId];
        if (!meta) return;
        lgIds.forEach(function (lg) {
            // THREE fixed figures, one per cell of the (lines x choice) grid
            // that actually matters. There is no mode to switch, because the
            // headline used to be the permissive one and read as though the kit
            // could ship in quantities it cannot:
            //   res     all lines, DEFAULT choices  — the kit as configured.
            //           The honest headline, and the .jrxml's number.
            //   exclOpt required lines only         — what you get if the
            //           optional lines are simply left off the order.
            //   best    all lines, BEST choices     — ship the optional lines,
            //           but pick the best-stocked product on each.
            var res     = computeKit(kitId, lg, true,  false);
            var proj    = computeKit(kitId, lg, true,  true);
            var exclOpt = computeKit(kitId, lg, false, false);
            var best    = computeKitBest(kitId, lg, false);
            _constraintByKey[kitId + '|' + lg] = new Set(res.constraint.map(function (c) { return c.partid; }));
            _bestByKey[kitId + '|' + lg] = best;
            var consNames = res.constraint.map(function (c) { return c.partnum; });
            var exclNames = exclOpt.constraint.map(function (c) { return c.partnum; });
            _allRows.push({
                kitproductid: kitId, lgid: lg,
                locationgroup: lgNameById(lg),
                kitnum: meta.kitnum, kitdesc: meta.kitdesc,
                qtyavailable: res.qty,
                qtyexcloptional: exclOpt.qty,
                qtybestvariation: best.qty,
                _bestSwaps: best.swaps,
                _bestContended: best.contended,
                qtyafterincoming: proj.qty,
                constraint: consNames.join(', '),     // filter / CSV / export value
                _constraintParts: consNames,          // for the compact constraint cell
                _exclConstraintParts: exclNames,      // tooltip on the Excl. Optional cell
                // Which optional line(s) are capping the kit, if any — that is
                // the whole reason Excl. Optional can exceed the headline.
                _optCapping: res.constraint.filter(function (c) {
                    var l = (_linesByKit[kitId] || []).find(function (x) { return x.partid === c.partid; });
                    return l && LINE_OPTIONAL.indexOf(l.linetypeid) !== -1;
                }).map(function (c) { return c.partnum; }),
                linecount: (_linesByKit[kitId] || []).length,
                kitprice: meta.kitprice,
                availablevalue: (res.qty != null ? res.qty * (meta.kitprice || 0) : null)
            });
        });
    });
}

async function loadDashboard() {
    var tok = ++_loadToken;
    debugLog('loadDashboard [' + tok + ']: start', 'info');
    document.getElementById('statusLine').textContent = 'Loading…';
    if (_lgMs) _setUserKey('lgSel', _lgMs.getSelected());

    function _empty(msg) {
        _allRows = []; _dataset = []; _linesByKit = {}; _optionsByLine = {};
        _kitMetaById = {}; _availMap = {}; _constraintByKey = {}; _bestByKey = {};
        _expanded.clear();
        if (_table) _table.render();
        _syncDetails();
        document.getElementById('statusLine').textContent = msg;
    }

    try {
        var lgIds = selectedLgIds();
        if (!lgIds.length) { _empty('No accessible location group'); return; }

        // 1) Kit products.
        var hdr = await runQueryP(buildKitHeaderSQL());
        if (tok !== _loadToken) return;
        var kitIds = [];
        _kitMetaById = {};
        hdr.slice(0, CAP_KITS).forEach(function (r) {
            var kid = parseInt(r.kitproductid, 10);
            if (!kid || _kitMetaById[kid]) return;
            _kitMetaById[kid] = { kitnum: r.kitnum || '', kitdesc: r.kitdesc || '', kitprice: num(r.kitprice) };
            kitIds.push(kid);
        });
        var limitHit = hdr.length > CAP_KITS;
        if (!kitIds.length) { _empty('No kits match the current filters'); return; }

        // 2) Kit lines. A LEFT JOIN on kitoption could in principle duplicate a
        //    line if two options were both flagged default, so dedupe by
        //    kititemid and keep the first (kitoption is ordered default-first).
        var lineRows = await runQueryP(buildKitLineSQL(kitIds));
        if (tok !== _loadToken) return;
        _linesByKit = {};
        var seenLine = {};
        var lineIds = [];
        kitIds.forEach(function (k) { _linesByKit[k] = []; });
        lineRows.forEach(function (r) {
            var liid = parseInt(r.kititemid, 10);
            if (seenLine[liid]) return;
            seenLine[liid] = true;
            lineIds.push(liid);
            var kid = parseInt(r.kitproductid, 10);
            var l = {
                kitproductid: kid, kititemid: liid,
                sortorder: (r.sortorder == null ? 0 : parseInt(r.sortorder, 10) || 0),
                linetypeid: parseInt(r.linetypeid, 10), linetype: r.linetype || '',
                linedesc: r.linedesc || '',
                isoptiongroup: truthy(r.isoptiongroup),
                productid: parseInt(r.productid, 10) || 0, productnum: r.productnum || '',
                partid: parseInt(r.partid, 10) || 0, partnum: r.partnum || '',
                partdesc: r.partdesc || '', parttype: parseInt(r.parttype, 10) || 0,
                partuom: r.partuom || '', kituom: r.kituom || '',
                kitqty: num(r.kitqty),
                convok: truthy(r.convok),
                multiply: num(r.multiply) || 1, factor: num(r.factor) || 1
            };
            (_linesByKit[kid] = _linesByKit[kid] || []).push(l);
        });

        // 3) Selectable alternatives for those lines (drill only).
        _optionsByLine = {};
        if (lineIds.length) {
            try {
                var opts = await runQueryP(buildKitOptionSQL(lineIds));
                if (tok !== _loadToken) return;
                opts.forEach(function (r) {
                    var liid = parseInt(r.kititemid, 10);
                    (_optionsByLine[liid] = _optionsByLine[liid] || []).push({
                        kititemid: liid,
                        isdefault: truthy(r.isdefault),
                        productid: parseInt(r.productid, 10) || 0, productnum: r.productnum || '',
                        partid: parseInt(r.partid, 10) || 0, partnum: r.partnum || '',
                        partdesc: r.partdesc || '', parttype: parseInt(r.parttype, 10) || 0,
                        partuom: r.partuom || ''
                    });
                });
            } catch (e) { debugLog('kitoption query failed: ' + e.message, 'warn'); }
        }

        // 4) Availability per part+LG for every part reachable from a kit line —
        //    including the alternatives, so the drill can price a swap.
        var partIdSet = {};
        Object.keys(_linesByKit).forEach(function (k) {
            _linesByKit[k].forEach(function (l) { if (l.partid) partIdSet[l.partid] = true; });
        });
        Object.keys(_optionsByLine).forEach(function (k) {
            _optionsByLine[k].forEach(function (o) { if (o.partid) partIdSet[o.partid] = true; });
        });
        var partIds = Object.keys(partIdSet).map(function (x) { return parseInt(x, 10); });
        _availMap = {};
        if (partIds.length) {
            var av = await runQueryP(buildAvailabilitySQL(partIds, lgIds));
            if (tok !== _loadToken) return;
            av.forEach(function (r) {
                var onhand = num(r.onhand), allocated = num(r.allocated),
                    notavail = num(r.notavail), dropship = num(r.dropship);
                var raw = onhand - allocated - notavail + dropship;
                _availMap[r.partid + '|' + r.lgid] = {
                    // Available for Sale, floored at 0 per location group.
                    available: Math.max(0, raw),
                    // The UNFLOORED figure is kept because Consolidated scope
                    // must sum raw and floor once — a group can be NEGATIVE
                    // (more allocated than on hand) and the .jrxml lets that
                    // shortfall eat into other groups' real stock.
                    rawavail: raw,
                    onhand: onhand,
                    // The components are kept so the breakdown can say WHICH of
                    // them zeroed a line — "in QA Hold" and "all committed to
                    // picks" and "over-promised on open orders" are three very
                    // different answers that all render as Available 0.
                    allocated: allocated,
                    notavail: notavail,
                    dropship: dropship,
                    committed: 0,           // filled by the committed query below
                    onorder: num(r.onorder)
                };
            });

            // Committed, from tag x location (see buildCommittedSQL).
            try {
                var cm = await runQueryP(buildCommittedSQL(partIds, lgIds));
                if (tok !== _loadToken) return;
                cm.forEach(function (r) {
                    var e = _availMap[r.partid + '|' + r.lgid];
                    if (e) e.committed = num(r.committed);
                });
            } catch (e) { debugLog('committed query failed: ' + e.message, 'warn'); }

            // Consolidated pseudo-LG. Summing RAW and flooring ONCE reproduces
            // the .jrxml exactly, including the netting: demodb part 11857 is
            // +23 in Melbourne and -9 in Brisbane, so consolidated availability
            // is 14, not the 23 Melbourne can actually supply. That is why the
            // Bearing Kit reads 7 consolidated and 11 in Melbourne.
            partIds.forEach(function (pid) {
                var raw = 0, oh = 0, oo = 0, al = 0, na = 0, ds = 0, cm = 0, seen = false;
                lgIds.forEach(function (lg) {
                    var a = _availMap[pid + '|' + lg];
                    if (!a) return;
                    seen = true;
                    raw += a.rawavail; oh += a.onhand; oo += a.onorder;
                    al += a.allocated; na += a.notavail; ds += a.dropship; cm += a.committed;
                });
                if (!seen) return;
                _availMap[pid + '|' + LG_ALL] = {
                    available: Math.max(0, raw), rawavail: raw, onhand: oh, onorder: oo,
                    allocated: al, notavail: na, dropship: ds, committed: cm
                };
            });
        }

        // 5) Build the summary rows. Whatever was expanded stays expanded: the
        //    reconciler rebuilds each breakdown from the freshly loaded lines
        //    and availability, so a refresh updates open panels in place rather
        //    than collapsing the user's place in the report.
        _rebuildRows();
        _populateValueFilters();
        _applyClientFilters();
        if (_table) _table.render();
        _syncDetails();
        document.getElementById('statusLine').innerHTML =
            _statusText() + (limitHit ? ' · capped at ' + CAP_KITS + ' kits' : '');
        debugLog('Computed ' + _allRows.length + ' rows across ' + kitIds.length + ' kit(s) x ' + lgIds.length + ' LG(s)', 'success');
    } catch (e) {
        debugLog('loadDashboard error: ' + (e && e.message), 'error');
        document.getElementById('statusLine').textContent = 'Error — see debug console';
    }
}

// ============================================================================
//  INLINE KIT-LINE EXPANSION
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  FBLib.Table owns the tbody: it re-renders it wholesale on sort/filter and
//  appends further chunks on scroll (lazy render), and it offers no detail-row
//  hook. So expansion is kept OUTSIDE the table as a set of row keys, and a
//  reconciler re-derives the DOM after any change the table makes:
//
//    _expanded        the source of truth — Set of "kitproductid|lgid"
//    _syncDetails()   strip every detail row, then re-insert one after each
//                     expanded summary row, and re-stamp keys + zebra striping
//    MutationObserver calls it whenever the table touches the tbody
//
//  Rebuilding the detail HTML each pass is cheap (a handful of lines per kit)
//  and removes a whole class of stale-DOM bugs; the lazy renderer bounds how
//  many summary rows are ever in the DOM, so "expand all" stays bounded too.
// ============================================================================
var _expanded = new Set();   // "kitproductid|lgid" of every expanded kit row
var _rowObserver = null;

function _rowKey(r) { return r.kitproductid + '|' + r.lgid; }
function _tbodyEl() { return document.querySelector('#reportTable tbody'); }
function _visibleColCount() {
    return _table ? _table.getColumns().filter(function (c) { return c.vis !== false; }).length : 1;
}

// Reconcile detail rows + row classes against _expanded. The observer is
// disconnected across the mutation (and its queue dropped) so our own DOM
// writes cannot re-trigger it.
function _syncDetails() {
    var tb = _tbodyEl();
    if (!tb) return;
    if (_rowObserver) _rowObserver.disconnect();
    try {
        Array.prototype.slice.call(tb.querySelectorAll('tr.kit-detail'))
            .forEach(function (tr) { tr.parentNode.removeChild(tr); });

        var rows = _table ? _table.getVisibleRows() : [];
        var colspan = _visibleColCount();
        var i = 0;
        Array.prototype.slice.call(tb.children).forEach(function (tr) {
            var row = rows[i];
            // The empty-state placeholder has no backing row — leave it alone.
            if (!row) return;
            i++;
            var key = _rowKey(row);
            tr.classList.add('kit-row');
            tr.classList.toggle('row-alt', (i % 2) === 0);
            tr.dataset.rowKey = key;
            if (!_expanded.has(key)) { tr.classList.remove('is-open'); return; }
            tr.classList.add('is-open');
            var det = document.createElement('tr');
            det.className = 'kit-detail';
            det.dataset.rowKey = key;
            var td = document.createElement('td');
            td.colSpan = colspan;
            td.innerHTML = '<div class="kit-detail-wrap">' + _detailHtml(row) + '</div>';
            det.appendChild(td);
            if (tr.nextSibling) tb.insertBefore(det, tr.nextSibling); else tb.appendChild(det);
        });
    } finally {
        if (_rowObserver) { _rowObserver.takeRecords(); _rowObserver.observe(tb, { childList: true }); }
        _refreshExpandBtn();
    }
}

// Row click toggles the breakdown. Anything with its own behaviour is excluded:
